problem: Most VLN-CE methods rely on costly panoramic RGB-D cameras for 360° observation, which is impractical for real-world deployment; monocular limited-FOV cameras give much less environment perception and weaker links to the instruction.
motivation: Low-cost monocular cameras are more practical for real robots, but 'looking less' hurts navigation. The paper's premise is that monocular robots can compensate by 'thinking more': recovering wider views from past observations and grounding instruction semantics explicitly in spatial maps.
key_idea: Let a monocular VLN-CE agent 'Think More' by rendering panoramic novel views at each step with 3D Gaussian Splatting built from past observations, and by fusing occupancy-map spatial semantics with instruction textual semantics.
insight: Only the abstract was available, so no ablation evidence can be cited. The abstract implies that wider perception (rendered views) and instruction-occupancy semantic alignment are complementary ways to make up for limited FOV.
method: 3DGS-based panoramic generation: renders novel views at each step from the collection of past monocular observations to approximate panoramic perception
Occupancy-instruction semantics enhancement: integrates the spatial semantics of occupancy maps with the textual semantics of the language instruction to give transparent semantic connections
Monocular VLN-CE setting: limited-FOV monocular camera as a low-cost, practical setup ('Look Less, Think More')

setting.observation: monocular RGB camera with limited field of view (rendered panoramic views from 3DGS)
